# Portable chemical Langevin (SDE) goldens

Generated by `go run ./cmd/sde-goldens -o stochastic/testdata/sde`, the SDE
counterpart of `cmd/ssa-goldens` (`stochastic/testdata/portable/`). Same
portable-path randomness (SplitMix64 → xoshiro256\*\*), same five models
(`chain`, `sir`, `dimer`, `gates`, `coffeeshop`) and same per-model options
(horizon/samples/realizations/seed) as the SSA fixtures of the same name, so
the two golden sets describe identical nets under two different engines.

**Two of the five carry no series.** `stochastic.SimulateSDE` refuses a model
whose firing is gated in ways continuous diffusion cannot express — read
arcs, inhibitor arcs, non-kinetic inputs, a reachable capacity bound, or a
declared schedule (see `sde.go`'s `ChemicalLangevinAssumption` and
`Model.Gating()`). `gates` and `coffeeshop` both hit that refusal (`gates`
via its read/inhibitor/non-kinetic/capacity arcs by construction; `coffeeshop`
because its three restock transitions make `coffee_beans`/`milk`/`cups`'
capacities reachable). Their goldens record `"diverged": true` and the
engine's own `reason`/`caveats` strings rather than a fabricated series — that
refusal is itself the byte-exact contract for those two fixtures. `chain`,
`sir` and `dimer` are unconstrained mass-action nets and carry a normal
`expected.times`/`expected.series`/`expected.final`, shaped exactly like the
SSA goldens' `expected` section (per-place `values`/`stddev` arrays, one
entry per reported time point).

Regeneration is a deliberate act, never a test side effect. A golden that
changes is a finding about the engine, and is never fixed by running the
generator again.

Intended to be vendored into `pflow-rs` (and any other consumer) the same way
`stochastic/testdata/portable/*.json` already is — see `pflow-rs/go-pflow.lock`
and `pflow-rs/ROADMAP.md`'s Phase 1 tracking note on "SDE goldens" for the
mechanism once that side adds `sde/*.json` to its lock.
